meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots + dull skin**, I’d pick a **10% vitamin C serum** rather than jumping straight to a very high-strength formula.

### My top picks in India

### [Minimalist Vitamin C 10% Face Serum]()
*₹284*

**1. Minimalist Vitamin C 10% — best overall for beginners**  
It uses **10% Ethyl Ascorbic Acid + 1% Acetyl Glucosamine**, is fragrance-free, and is designed specifically for dullness, sun damage and dark spots. Current listed price is around **₹285**. [beminimalist.co](https://beminimalist.co/products/vitamin-c-ethyl-ascorbic-acid-10-acetyl-glucosamine-1?_pos=5&_sid=f990e0029&_ss=r&utm_source=chatgpt.com)  
**My pick if you haven't used vitamin C before.**

### [Deconstruct 10% Vitamin C + Ferulic Acid Serum]()
*₹458*

**2. Deconstruct 10% Vitamin C + 0.5% Ferulic Acid — best for pigmentation + dullness**  
The liposomal vitamin C formulation is designed for stability, while ferulic acid provides additional antioxidant support. It's fragrance-free and currently listed around **₹262–₹349**, depending on size/offer. [thedeconstruct.in](https://thedeconstruct.in/products/vitamin-c-and-ferulic-acid-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### [Dot & Key 10% Vitamin C + E + 5% Niacinamide]()
*₹278*

**3. Dot & Key 10% Vitamin C + E + 5% Niacinamide — best if you want multiple brightening ingredients**  
The combination targets dullness and pigmentation while niacinamide can help with uneven tone. [www.dotandkey.com](https://www.dotandkey.com/blogs/skin-care/dermatologist-recommended-face-serums-in-india?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd buy
**Minimalist 10%** if you're a beginner or have somewhat sensitive skin.  
**Deconstruct 10%** if dark spots/pigmentation are your main concern.

**Important:** vitamin C works much better as part of an AM routine with **SPF 50 sunscreen**. Otherwise, continued UV exposure can keep producing pigmentation. Consistency matters more than using an extremely strong serum. [www.whowhatwear.com](https://www.whowhatwear.com/beauty/skin/best-products-for-hyperpigmentation?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Start **3–4 mornings/week**, then increase to daily if your skin tolerates it. Patch-test first, and don't combine it initially with several other strong actives.

If you tell me your **skin type (oily/dry/combination/sensitive)** and **budget (₹300 / ₹500 / ₹1000+)**, I can narrow it down to **one exact serum** for you.

sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
